target_customer: Enterprises building internal AI agents and software companies embedding agents into products
problem: Enterprise agents lack organizational context and feedback, so they do not improve against outcomes the company cares about.
business_model: Enterprise platform with a forward deployed engineer offering; browser product Dex earlier
product_category: Enterprise AI agent platform and evaluation

founders.name: Regina Lin
education: Harvard, mathematics with concurrent master's in computational science, dropped out (YC page)
previous_startups: Contour AI (co-founded, LLM evaluation devops tool, outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: YC page also lists help building an ecommerce marketplace MVP.

founders.name: Kevin Gu
founders.background_notes: YC page bios describe Dex/Dexterity; his role at Thirdlayer is not explicitly confirmed.

competitors.name: Galileo
competitors.what: Agentic evaluations and observability for GenAI

technical_complexity.rationale: Context ingestion across permissioned data plus outcome grading and learning loops for agents is hard for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Crowded evaluation space with big platform players; value would come from deep integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Salesforce added a testing center for agents and others shipped agent evaluation in 2025; no acquisition of Thirdlayer found.

market_need_then: Enterprises were deploying agents in 2025 and agent evaluation products were launching, indicating demand, but sources checked give no spend data for this specific wedge.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise, outcome focused: Own the intelligence behind your operations.

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt listing for Dex; a YC-linked listing claims 10,000+ users as of January 2026 (unverified).

brand_strength.rationale: Little coverage of the brand itself; confusion between Dex, Dexterity and Thirdlayer on YC pages and a clash with unrelated Dexterity robotics.

pivots.from: Earlier product built during the batch (not described in sources)
pivots.to: Dex, an AI coworker in the browser
pivots.why: YC launch post says the team pivoted about four weeks before Demo Day; reason not found. Month approximate from batch timing.

pivots.to: Enterprise learning and alignment layer for agents
pivots.why: Current site and YC description; timing and reason not found.

outcome_analysis: Thirdlayer is active with two people. It pivoted at least twice, first to a browser copilot and then toward enterprise agent infrastructure, which shows search for a wedge rather than settled product market fit. No public funding beyond the standard YC deal was found, so it is too early to judge.
notes: An everydev.ai listing shows a $500,000 YC pre-seed (January 2025); aggregator only, unverified. An Extruct entry of a $75M Series C in 2023 is a different company and is discarded. Pivot dates are approximate. Competitor list is a category sample, not proven direct rivals, and the pivot to the enterprise positioning came later than the batch. Downgraded to depth 1 by orchestrator: the researcher reported skipping the separate outcome search and the funding cross-check, and removed undated competitors to clear warnings.
